authoredPrompt: This figure is part of a worked example that evaluates the line integral of F = cos(x) i + sin(x) j along two different oriented curves. The figure contains two panels (a) and (b), each showing the same vector field F drawn over a green-shaded background with the note Vectors not to scale. Panel (a): the oriented curve C is a short vertical red line segment at x = -pi/2, directed downards from y = 2 to y = 1. Panel (b): the oriented curve C is a parabolic arc from (-1, 1) to (2, 4), directed first down, then upward and to the right. The figure shows the two distinct integration paths for parts (a) and (b) of the example, making visible how each curve's geometry and alignment relative to the field vectors determines the computed line integral. Note that the two parts of the image are differently scaled.
authoredInteractions:
- Drag the endpoints of curve C to reshape the integration path through the vector field and watch the line integral value update in real time
- Toggle between the two panels (short vertical path vs. long curved path) to compare how path shape and length affect the line integral value over the same field
- Slider for parameter t: animate a moving point along C and display the field vector and its dot product with the tangent at each step

discrepancies: The vertical path (Path a) is reversed; the source figure shows the path going upwards from y=1 to y=2, but the generated figure defaults to downwards from y=2 to y=1.
The parabolic path (Path b) ends at y=4 in the generated figure, whereas the source figure shows it ending lower, exactly on the y=3 gridline.
The arrowheads on the vector field are drawn as filled triangles in the generated figure, while the source uses open V-shape strokes.
evaluation.notes: An exceptionally good interactive workbench that calculates real-time line integrals with draggable paths; the only notable flaw is that the default vertical path points in the opposite direction from the source.
action_items: Reverse the start and end coordinates for Path A in the default state so that P0 is at y=1 and P2 is at y=2, making the path point upwards to match the source.
Adjust the default End Point (P2) for Path B from (2, 4) to (2, 3) to better match the geometry of the source figure.
Change the vector field arrows to use simple open V-shaped strokes (polyline/lines) rather than filled polygons, matching the source's simpler aesthetic.
